description: The Transboundary Freshwater Diplomacy Database is the Oregon State University collection of information on how countries share rivers, lakes and aquifers, built and maintained by the College of Earth, Ocean, and Atmospheric Sciences with the Northwest Alliance for Computational Science and Engineering. The database page names six components: data, which holds global and regional searchable tabular and spatial datasets, treaty and compact libraries and downloadable GIS shapefiles; research and projects; bibliographies and digital collections, including a water conflict and cooperation bibliography; publications; map and image galleries; and external resource links. The data-use note says the data, coverages and findings are not copyrighted and that use is encouraged, with a credit line requested. Coverage: global, by international basin and treaty, with no single record count on the pages read. Access: free web tables and downloads. Caveats: this record was built from the programme and database pages, not from the individual datasets, and the site is being rebuilt so links may move. It supplies basin boundaries and treaty context for scenarios about shared reservoirs, flow allocation and cross-border flood or drought cooperation, and relates to the dam and basin records already catalogued.
